title: Day 660 — USMCA Round 3 Talks Conclude in Mexico City; Progress Reported on Autos, Steel, Labor as Fourth Round Set for September in Washington
detail: From July 21–23, 2026 (through Day 660, Thursday), Mexican and U.S. negotiators held a third round of bilateral talks in Mexico City related to the joint review of the USMCA, with Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard's team meeting U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer's delegation. The round came three weeks after USTR Ambassador Greer's July 1 statement that the United States would not renew the USMCA in its current form, meaning the agreement stayed in force but entered the treaty's rolling annual-review mechanism rather than securing a clean 16-year extension through 2042. According to a joint statement, the two sides reported progress on a shared agenda covering economic security, labor standards, agriculture, electronic payment services, steel and aluminum tariffs and their derivative products, and the automotive sector — though no binding agreements were signed. Sheinbaum's government continued pressing for zero tariffs on USMCA-compliant vehicles and a rollback of the 50% steel and aluminum duties, which Ebrard's team has called indefensible. A fourth round of negotiations was scheduled for the week of September, 2026 in Washington, D.C.

sources.name: Office of the U.S. Trade Representative

media.caption: Mexico and the US wrap up the third round of USMCA joint-review talks in Mexico City
